title: Containers, CI and cloud
why: A project that only runs on your laptop doesn't count. Employers want to click a link, and they look for CI as a sign you work like an engineer.
outcomes: Write a slim Dockerfile for a Python service
Run the service and Postgres together with docker compose
Test on every push with GitHub Actions
Deploy to Render and once to Azure, with secrets set in the platform
lessons: Docker basics: images, containers, layers, a slim Python Dockerfile
docker compose: your API plus Postgres with pgvector
GitHub Actions: lint, type-check and test on every push
Deploy the APIs module's service to Render's free tier with secrets in the dashboard
Open an Azure free account and deploy once to Azure Container Apps
Read logs, add a health check, document cold starts in the README
resources: Images, containers, Compose and volumes, explained with diagrams.
GitHub Actions Tutorial: CI/CD with Docker
A workflow that tests and builds on every push.
method: Deploy early and ugly, then improve. The first deploy of every project happens in its first week, not its last.
build: Your APIs-module service, containerised, tested by CI and live at a public URL, with a status badge in the README.

o: An image is the blueprint; a container is a running instance of it
quiz.e: You build an image once and run many containers from it.

quiz.q: Why pin dependency versions with a lockfile?
o: Reproducible builds: the same versions everywhere
quiz.e: Pinning stops a silent upstream release breaking your deploy.

quiz.q: At minimum, a CI pipeline should:
o: Run tests and lint on every push
quiz.e: Automatic checks on every push catch breakage before it ships.

o: It works on my machine but nowhere else
quiz.e: The container carries its dependencies, so it runs the same everywhere.

quiz.q: Your free-tier app sleeps when idle. What should you do?
o: Note the cold-start delay in the README so reviewers expect it
Remove the link from your CV
quiz.e: Owning the limitation reads as professional; a silent 30-second wait reads as broken.
